chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Tuning, matching vibrato and breathing together
summary: The reed men matched tone and vibrato to the lead player and marked where to breathe, so phrases sounded as one.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone

Everybody had good tone. Everybody had good solid tone -- clear tones. They're good musicians, good reed men -- what you call reed men.
Now, what we would do the first few minutes, we'd be, (inaudible) before we played anything. We would be tuning up, matching our vibratos together.
You hit a whole note to see if it matches. Everybody (matchin' inaudible) -- we would hit a chord, you know.
Then we'd tune up (inaudible). Then we try something out, you know. A few bars, to see if we got the right blend -- (It what inaudible) you did in the big bands, too.
When you come into a band, you have to either get together the first alto piece, see where he's at and you match your vibrato (inaudible).

That's another thing. When you're playing a solo -- when you're playing something, they mark where they gonna breathe. Everybody breathe together.
